promotions.set_note: The corpus's way of recording the priority literature without adjudicating it: Poincaré's contribution is real and documented, and it is influence rather than founding. enwiki Relativity priority dispute states that Einstein's publications "referred only to a small number of his predecessors for fundamental results on which he based his theories, most notably to the work of Henri Poincaré and Hendrik Lorentz for special relativity". Hendrik Lorentz is named in the same breath and now carries his own edge, edge:hendrik-lorentz-influenced-theory-of-relativity, on the same `influenced` disposition — the gap this note recorded is closed. This edge is also what makes the concept admissible at all: it was rejected in concept-wave3-v1 precisely because Poincaré would have been its only person link. [Note refreshed 2026-07-30, decision (118): the sentence above replaced a recorded gap that had gone false. The claim, its sources and its confidence are unchanged.]

notes: Stale-note refresh. Three `reviewed` edges carried honest-gap prose that had gone false: each said a co-founder was 'not yet a node' / 'not a corpus node', and in all three cases the person node AND the co-founder edge were admitted by later waves (Peirce, Koch, Virchow — and now Remak alongside Virchow). Recorded gaps are load-bearing in this corpus: they are how the next wave's slate gets built, and a gap that silently closed is worse than no gap, because a reader trusts it.

★ Two of the six were made stale BY THIS SESSION: person-wave12 admitted Lorentz and Remak, which silently falsified the gap notes on edge:henri-poincare-influenced-theory-of-relativity and edge:rudolf-virchow-founded-cell-theory that named them. That is the systematic hazard here — admitting a node falsifies every recorded gap that named it, in the same commit, invisibly. The first pass of this batch missed both because it worked from a hand-built list of three; a name-to-node scan found them. A third case (Duncan Black on edge:kenneth-arrow-founded-social-choice-theory) had been stale since before this session and nobody had noticed.

★ The seventh entry was found by the detector this batch ships, not by hand: a manual scan caught Duncan Black on edge:kenneth-arrow-founded-social-choice-theory and missed the identical stale sentence on edge:amartya-sen-founded-social-choice-theory. The detector earned its place before it was committed.

Surfaced by the session #61 closeout audit's next-work inventory, which also flagged three FALSE positives worth not re-chasing — those same three notes are the whole set; no other edge note in /data claims a missing referent that now exists (re-checked this session).

Shape: reviewed→reviewed metadata flips carrying set_note only, the CPO-ratified path (2026-07-02, session #55 ext.). No ladder sanction is demanded and none is claimed: nothing (re)earns reviewed here. Each refreshed note states what it replaced and why, so the correction is auditable from the note itself rather than only from this file.

One live gap deliberately preserved: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, co-credited in the Pasteur note for early microscopy, is still absent from the corpus. The refreshed note keeps that gap explicit instead of dropping the sentence wholesale.

[NO-EXTERNAL-EVIDENCE] This batch makes no factual claim and reads no external page: every quote in every refreshed note is carried over verbatim from the note it replaces, and the claims those quotes support were verified when the edges were promoted. The only new assertions are about corpus state (which node/edge ids exist), verified by reading /data.
